summary: S04 v2 'Frame the subject' is built and QA'd at preview, with a final-mode cost probe. f1-30 are v1 (camera keys f0-30 bit-identical; pixels at the GPU's run-to-run noise floor at preview and final). One log-distance push from f31 runs to x7.000 (frame height 0.496 of the canvas, 6.1 texels/px, square, f/11), centred on uv (0.486, 0.637). The SETTLE peaks at x7.42 on the f136 beat and comes to rest at f149. f150-180 is a static hold, with identical keys and pixel differences at dither level. There is no orb, no dot-pop, no bloom. The --overscan still is checked at preview and final; final crop vs f180: mean 0.61/255, p99 2.56/255 after a 1 px blur. Final cost is 7.1 s/frame on GPU 6 alone: 0.39 GPU-h for 180 frames in the queue's 3 jobs, plus 0.016 GPU-h for the overscan still (cap 0.45). This session (it continued an interrupted build): re-checked the preview QA, measured the clean final cost, fixed a wrong docstring claim (peak margins), documented the --overscan interface, added cost_final / zoom_end / built_mode to the meta (rebuilt in final mode) and checked the interface against scripts/render_finals.py --film v2 (they agree). Lead follow-up (17:00-17:50): the overscan's mirror extension, which folded trunks into V/diamond shapes, is replaced by a generated pointillist foliage band. scripts/make_seurat_ext.py (CPU, deterministic, seed 7) writes assets/paintings/derived/seurat_grande_jatte_{20000,8192,2048}_topband.png + seurat_grande_jatte_ext.json. In --overscan the shader keeps the original JPEG for v <= 0.9365 (the whole f180 frame and everything below it) and cross-fades to the band above. The band has no mirrored structure and no seam, and it hides the painted border. Preview overscan re-rendered, crop QA unchanged (mean 0.784/255, p99 3.06); hex tile c_painting refreshed. f_0001-0180 are unchanged (a re-rendered preview f180 matches within GPU noise).

deviations: SETTLE overshoot is +6 % in image scale (x7.42 -> x7.00, 2.9 % of the log move); 6 % of the log move would be +12 % in scale and cut the parasol tip.
SETTLE shaped in closed form (ease_in_out_sine forward lobe + sin^2 return lobe) instead of D.spring, so the move ends exactly at f149 and f150-180 are static.
Subject centre moved by (0, +0.004) uv from the storyboard (0.486, 0.633) after the f180 framing test (allowed <= 0.02).
At the one-frame push peak the parasol-tip margin is 2.8 % (the >= 3 % rule holds at the end framing: 5.5 % / 5.6 %).
'No emission anywhere' vs 'f1-30 bit-for-bit': v1's lamp bulb (emissive, inside the translucent shade) is kept, because it is part of the f1-30 set; it is off-frame from ~f55.
Focus hands off from v1's dot depth to the subject over f30-46 (sub-pixel; f1-30 keep v1's focus exactly).

Overscan extension: a generated foliage band (scripts/make_seurat_ext.py) instead of the storyboard's MIRROR texture extension. Any mirror repeats the trunks as chevrons. The band is written separately rather than as a full painting+band image, so the original JPEG (Blender's own decode) is used for v <= 0.9365 and the painting inside the f180 frame is untouched. The feather is wider than the suggested 1-2 %: patches cover the painting from v 0.945-0.960 to full at v 0.971-0.9795, ~1.5-3.5 % varying along u, so the trunks do not all end on one line. The hex top is 14.3 % of the canvas height above the painting (storyboard ~13 %).
open_issues: render_finals.py --film v2 interleaves s04_subject over 3 processes (1-178:3, ...), so consecutive hold frames come from different processes. They are identical only up to GPU run-to-run noise (mean ~0.04/255, sparse max ~5/255). That is far inside qa_finals' 0.5/255 rule, but not bit-identical. Rendering f150-180 in one job (or copying f150) would make the hold bit-identical. That is the post-tools builder's file.

The final overscan needs assets/paintings/derived/seurat_grande_jatte_20000_topband.png (now on disk; regenerate with tools/venv/bin/python -I scripts/make_seurat_ext.py, ~2 min CPU, ~20 GB RAM). docs/shots_v2.json asset_deps does not list it (not my file). The script stops with that hint if the band is missing.

scripts/make_hex_tiles.py's painting placeholder (used only when no overscan.png exists) reads overscan.texture_extension.mirror_above_v. That key is gone, so the placeholder falls back to a plain mirror at v 1.0. It could read the band PNG instead (hex-tiles builder's file). The real still is correct.
renders/final/s04_subject/overscan.png does not exist yet (rendered by the finals queue; not rendered here, per the lead).
notes_for_critic: Look at renders/review/s04_subject_sheet.png, then at preview f136 (push peak) and f180 (hold = finale f1). The settle reads as a soft landing over f132-149: the push passes x7.0 at f127.6, peaks at x7.42 on the beat and eases back. The frame-diff 'dip' at f135-137 in qa_preview.json is the designed reversal, not a hitch. The f76-82 dip in the optical-flow p90 is the textureless lemon wall filling the frame; the analytic wall-plane flow is one smooth lobe. The f1-30 identity is proved two ways: the camera keys from both scripts are bit-identical, and the pixel differences equal those between two renders of the v1 script itself (GPU noise). The cost numbers come only from frames rendered while GPU 6 ran no other process. If you want >= 3 % margins even at the peak frame, set OVER = 0.0355 (+5.5 % overshoot; needs a preview re-render of f32-148). If the overscan chevrons read in the finale's first second, see open_issues[0]. Script edits in this session were docstring and meta only (no render input changed), so the preview frames from 16:13-16:18 are current. Overscan follow-up: compare renders/work/s04_subject/ovs_top_before_after.png. The band is synthesised from the canopy's own brushwork: elliptical patches 12-34 texels across, foliage-only, colour-matched to soft masses. Near the old painting edge the masses are the painting's own foliage low-pass, reflected (trunks masked out), so nothing at a recognisable scale is mirrored. At 1:1 on the 20000 scan the transition into the band is not visible.
